contentBody:
Ananya installs Tailwind in a Vite React app and writes this JSX: ```jsx
Mess open
``` The words stay on a plain, uncoloured background. Which missing step is the most likely cause?
option.2: Colour utilities also need an inline `style` attribute to work
option.4: `npm install` alone turns every utility on, so the import is optional
answerExplanation:
C is correct because installing the packages is not enough. The CSS file that the app already imports must contain `@import "tailwindcss"`. Without that line, names such as `bg-green-500` sit in the JSX and draw no colour.

A is incorrect because React uses `className`, not `class`. Switching to `class` would make the situation worse. B is incorrect because a colour utility stands on its own; a separate `style` attribute is not required. D is incorrect because `npm install` only downloads the packages. Vite still needs the plugin, and `index.css` still needs the import.

contentBody:
A hostel notice card uses this markup: ```jsx
Quiet hours
``` How much inner space does `p-4` add around the words?
answerExplanation:
B is correct because the number in `p-4` is a step on Tailwind’s scale, not a raw pixel count. Step `4` is 1rem, which is 16 pixels, and `p` with no side letter applies that space on all four sides.

A is incorrect because step `1` is 4 pixels. Reading `4` as 4 pixels is a common slip. C is incorrect because `p-4` is not left-only padding, and the step is not 4rem. D is incorrect because top-only padding is `pt-4`.

contentBody: Kabir wants to attach Tailwind utilities to a React `h1`. Which attribute must he write on that element?
answerExplanation:
A is correct because JSX already uses `class` as a reserved word in JavaScript. The attribute that holds utility classes is `className`, with a capital N.

B is incorrect because `class` is the HTML name, not the React attribute. C and D are incorrect because they are not the React attribute for CSS classes.

contentBody:
A canteen heading is written like this: ```jsx

Hello

``` What does `text-blue-600` change?
option.4: The font size of the heading
answerExplanation:
C is correct because a colour utility names the role first. `text-` colours the letters. Shade `600` is a strong blue.

A is incorrect because the background role is `bg-`, as in `bg-blue-600`. B is incorrect because a border colour needs `border` plus a class such as `border-blue-600`. D is incorrect because size is `text-3xl`. `text-blue-600` does not set the size.

contentBody: A library slip needs 16 pixels of padding on the left and the right only. The top and bottom should stay tight. Which class matches that request?
answerExplanation:
A is correct because `x` is the horizontal axis. `px-4` is left and right padding at step `4`, which is 16 pixels.

B is incorrect because `py-4` is top and bottom. C is incorrect because `p-4` pads every side. D is incorrect because `pt-4` pads only the top.

contentBody: Meera already has a working name screen. The input uses `useState`, `value`, and `onChange`. She only adds Tailwind classes such as `mt-4 w-full p-3 border rounded-lg` on that input. What happens to the state logic?
option.1: `useState` is replaced, so typing no longer updates the greeting
option.2: `value` and `onChange` must be removed for the utilities to apply
option.3: The look changes; the stored name and the re-render stay
option.4: `rounded-lg` stores the typed name, so `setName` is no longer used
answerExplanation:
C is correct because Tailwind only changes appearance through `className`. `useState`, `value`, and `onChange` keep working. A state update still re-renders the component.

A is incorrect because adding classes does not replace React state. B is incorrect because those two attributes are what make the box controlled; they are not in the way of utilities. D is incorrect because `rounded-lg` only curves the corners. It does not store text.

contentBody: Which of the following statements about Tailwind spacing are true?
option.1: `p-4` adds 16 pixels of padding on all four sides
option.2: `p-4` adds 4 pixels of padding on all four sides
option.3: `p-6` adds 24 pixels of padding on all four sides
option.4: `m-4` is the class for padding inside the box
option.5: `px-4` adds 16 pixels of padding on the left and the right
answerExplanation:
A is correct because `p` with no side letter is every side, and step `4` is 16 pixels. C is correct because step `6` is 1.5rem, which is 24 pixels. E is correct because `x` is left and right, still at step `4`.

B is incorrect because 4 pixels is step `1`, not step `4`. D is incorrect because `m` is margin, the gap outside the box. Padding uses `p`.

contentBody: A hostel notice bar should show `Hostel` at one end and `Profile` at the other end of a single horizontal row. Which utilities must sit on that parent so the two labels are pushed to opposite ends?
answerExplanation:
A is correct because `flex` turns the parent into a flex container. The default direction is a horizontal row. B is correct because `justify-between` pushes the first child to one end and the last child to the other end.

C is incorrect because `flex-col` stacks the labels top to bottom, so they are not at opposite ends of a row. D is incorrect because `pt-4` only adds top padding. E is incorrect because `text-3xl` only changes font size.

contentBody:
A campus page uses this parent: ```jsx
Main content
Side panel
``` Which statements are true?
option.1: On a 500 pixel phone, the two panels stack in a column
option.2: From 768 pixels upward, the two panels sit side by side in a row
option.3: `md:flex-row` applies on every width, including a narrow phone
option.5: The unprefixed `flex-col` is the small-screen layout
answerExplanation:
A is correct because Tailwind is mobile first. With no matching `md:` prefix on a 500 pixel screen, `flex-col` stays in charge, so the panels stack. B is correct because `md:` starts at 768 pixels, and `md:flex-row` then switches the same parent to a row. E is correct because classes with no prefix are the phone style.

C is incorrect because a prefixed class joins in only from that breakpoint upward. A narrow phone keeps the column. D is incorrect because `gap-4` has no prefix, so the 16 pixel gap applies at every width.

contentBody: Riya restyles a working Welcome card. She keeps `useState` and the controlled input. The outer box uses `max-w-md mx-auto mt-10 p-6 bg-white rounded-lg shadow`. The greeting paragraph uses `text-base sm:text-lg`. The main line of the card also uses `className="text-2xl font-bold text-slate-800"`. Which statements are true?
option.1: `mx-auto` centres the width-capped card with equal left and right margins
option.2: `p-6` is 24 pixels of padding inside the card
option.3: `sm:text-lg` enlarges the greeting from 640 pixels upward
option.4: `text-2xl` and `font-bold` are the same class, so one of them can be dropped
option.5: Adding these classes replaces `useState`, so the greeting stops updating
answerExplanation:
A is correct because `max-w-md` caps the width and `mx-auto` centres that box. B is correct because step `6` is 1.5rem, which is 24 pixels, and `p` applies it on every side. C is correct because `sm:` starts at 640 pixels, so the greeting stays `text-base` on a narrower phone and becomes `text-lg` from that width up.

D is incorrect because size and weight are separate. `text-2xl` only changes size. `font-bold` only changes weight. E is incorrect because restyling changes `className` only. The stored name and the re-render stay as they were.

contentBody:
The hostel mess already has a working name slip. Typing a name updates the greeting at once. The slip behaves correctly, but it still looks plain.

Your job is to keep that behaviour and dress the slip with Tailwind utilities only. Do not write a new `.css` rule for this card. Do not replace `useState`.

## Task

Create a single file named `MessTokenCard.jsx`.

Build one component named `MessTokenCard` that holds this state:

| State | Starts as | What it stores |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `""` | Text in the name box |

The screen must include:

1. An outer card whose `className` is exactly `max-w-md mx-auto mt-10 p-6 bg-white rounded-lg shadow`.
2. A heading whose text is `Mess token` and whose `className` is exactly `text-2xl font-bold text-slate-800`.
3. A name input whose displayed text is `name`. Typing in it updates `name`. Its `className` is exactly `mt-4 w-full p-3 border rounded-lg`. Its placeholder is `Enter your name`.
4. A greeting line that uses a ternary:
   - If `name` is `""`, show `Please enter your name`.
   - Otherwise show `Hello, ` followed by the stored name.
   - The greeting paragraph `className` is exactly `mt-4 text-slate-600`.
5. Under the greeting, a row with two short labels whose visible text is `Counter` and `Token`. That row’s `className` is exactly `flex flex-col justify-between gap-4 mt-4 md:flex-row`.

Do not add extra buttons. Do not add a second name. The React logic stays in this one component. Styling must use the class lists above, not a separate stylesheet for the card.

## Sample walkthrough

Check the screen in this order. The input shows the stored text after each step. Resize the browser when a check mentions width.

### Check A — page just opened

| On screen | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Name box | empty |
| Heading | `Mess token` |
| Greeting line | `Please enter your name` |
| Row labels | `Counter` and `Token` |
| Card look | centred white card, 24px inner padding, 8px corners, drop shadow |

### Check B — type a name

Type `Kabir` into the name box.

| On screen | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Name box | `Kabir` |
| Greeting line | `Hello, Kabir` |
| Row labels | still `Counter` and `Token` |

### Check C — clear the name

Delete the text so the box is empty again.

| On screen | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Name box | empty |
| Greeting line | `Please enter your name` |

### Check D — narrow window

Set the window width below 768 pixels, for example 500 pixels.

| On screen | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `Counter` and `Token` | stacked in a column (`flex-col`) |

### Check E — wider window

Widen the window past 768 pixels.

| On screen | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `Counter` and `Token` | sit in one row (`md:flex-row`) |

If the greeting stops updating, put `value` and `onChange` back and leave the look in `className`.

## Submission instructions

- Code all the points above in VS Code in a single `MessTokenCard.jsx` file.
- Render `MessTokenCard` in your Vite React app (Tailwind already set up), run it, and verify Checks A to E.
- Submit the code in the code editor / answer box on the LMS.
answerExplanation:
### Walkthrough This card is the same kind of name screen as a controlled input, with Tailwind classes on the JSX. - `name` starts as `""`. The input’s `value` is that state, and `onChange` stores `event.target.value`. Typing still re-renders the component. The utilities on the input (`mt-4 w-full p-3 border rounded-lg`) only space, stretch, pad, and outline the box. - The greeting ternary is unchanged by Tailwind. An empty name shows `Please enter your name`. A typed name shows `Hello, ` plus that name. `mt-4 text-slate-600` only spaces and colours that line. - The outer card uses `max-w-md` so it does not stretch across a wide monitor, `mx-auto` to centre it, `mt-10` to drop it from the top, `p-6` for 24 pixels of inner space, then `bg-white`, `rounded-lg` (8 pixel corners), and `shadow`. - The heading uses size and weight as two classes: `text-2xl` and `font-bold`, plus `text-slate-800` for a dark colour. - The label row is mobile first. `flex flex-col` stacks `Counter` and `Token` on a phone. `md:flex-row` places them side by side from 768 pixels upward. `justify-between` and `gap-4` stay on at every width. No new CSS file is needed for these looks. If a class shows no effect in the host app, the usual setup check is the Vite plugin plus `@import "tailwindcss"` in `index.css`. ### Complete code ```jsx import { useState } from "react"; function MessTokenCard() { const [name, setName] = useState(""); return (
